newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BOBIC HOPES TO DO LEVERKUSEN A FAVOUR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BOBIC HOPES TO DO LEVERKUSEN A FAVOUR.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart striker Fredi Bobic is confident his side will give their all for a victory over Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich on Saturday, even though they have nothing left to play for in the league this season.

Stuttgart have already qualified for the UEFA Cup but can no longer make next season's Champions' League. They could therefore be forgiven for concentrating on next month's German Cup against regional league side Energie Cottbus.
But Bobic insisted Stuttgart would do their utmost against Bayern and admitted he would prefer Bayer Leverkusen, the only side who can catch the leaders, to win the league title.
"We have the chance to shoot Bayern off the top of the table and we want to use that chance," he said.
With two games left, Bayern are a point clear of Leverkusen who take on local rivals Cologne on Saturday.

A win for Bayern and anything less than three points for Leverkusen would hand the Munich club their 14th Bundesliga title. But if Stuttgart were to beat Bayern, Leverkusen could find themselves in the driving seat.

Stuttgart will be weakened by the loss of former Germany defender Thomas Berthold who is suspended. But coach Joachim Loew can welcome back midfielder Andreas Buck from injury and Marco Haber in defence after suspension.

Bayern coach Gioanni Trapattoni is also worried about a veteran defender -- Lothar Matthaeus. The World Cup-winning libero is doubtful with a muscle strain, while midfielder Thomas Strunz is definitely out with a back problem.
Bobic's Brazilian strike partner Giovane Elber faces a difficult afternoon in the Olympic Stadium.
Elber joins Bayern at the end of the season, prompting suggestions he may be reluctant to score a goal against his future employers which could deprive them of the championship.
But Bobic insists Elber is just going through a normal slump in form.
"Giovane has nothing to be ashamed of. He always gives 100 percent and puts in a top performance, even when he doesn't score," he said.
"Of course, he's looking forward to his new job in Munich. But until June 14 he'll give everything to Stuttgart. I hope he crowns a good season with a goal on Saturday."
The man Elber is replacing at Bayern, Germany captain Juergen Klinsmann, agrees with Bobic.

"Giovane's enough of a professional," said Klinsmann who will join Italian club Sampdoria in the close season. "He'll give complete commitment to Stuttgart right to the end. He's got a lot to thank the club for."

Bayern - 1-Oliver Kahn, 10-Lothar Matthaeus, 5-Thomas Helmer, 2-Markus Babbel, 7-Mario Basler, 11-Marcel Witeczek, 7-Mehmet Scholl, 6-Christian Nerlinger, 17-Christian Ziege, 18-Juergen Klinsmann, 20-Ruggiero Rizzitelli.

Stuttgart - 1-Franz Wohlfahrt, 8-Marco Haber, 5-Frank Verlaat, 14-Thomas Schneider, 22-Andreas Buck, 12-Danny Schwarz, 10-Krasimir Balakov, 7-Matthias Hagner, 16-Gerhard Poschner, 9-Giovane Elber, 11-Fredi Bobic.
